newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends lower, feed grains end mixed.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends lower, feed grains end mixed.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed lower, largely reflecting declines in CBOT soybeans and soybean oil, traders said.

Selling pressure may have been fueled by market talk a Canada canola processing plant temporarily suspended operations. A reason for the suspension was not mentioned, but traders said poor crushing margins may be to blame.
WCE November canola closed down $7.50 at $420.70 per tonne.
Flaxseed futures closed slightly lower hedge selling was opposed by light commercial buying. October flaxseed closed off $1.00 at $398.50.
Feed grains were mixed with shortcovering lifting October wheat, which closed up $2.00 at $174.00 per tonne.
November western barley rose $1.00 to $146.00, with commission house buying countered by local selling. October feed peas closed down $2.50 at $199.00 and October oats were off $0.50 at $136.50.
The Canadian dollar was quoted at about $1.3514 against the U.S. dollar.
(All values in Canadian dollars except for feed peas and oats which are in U.S. dollars).
